title: FEAST: Fair and Efficient Adaptive Sampling for Task-Free On-Policy Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.33827v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Language agents trained from self-generated experience must allocate a limited rollout budget across heterogeneous capabilities. A common strategy is to prioritize capabilities with strong current learning signals, but in on-policy learning these signals are endogenous: past allocation changes the policy and therefore the evidence available for future allocation. This can create a feedback loop in which under-trained capabilities receive increasingly fewer opportunities to improve. We formalize this effect through the Quota-Efficiency Law (QEL), which shows that allocation history can change learning efficiency even under matched capability-specific exposure. Motivated by this, we introduce FEAST, a task-free adaptive sampling framework that separates opportunity allocation from compute allocation. FEAST dynamically discovers capability clusters while preserving their learning histories, maintains continued sampling opportunities acros

translated_title: FEAST：面向无任务在线策略学习的公平高效自适应采样
translated_abstract: 从自生成经验中训练的语言智能体必须在异构能力之间分配有限的 rollout 预算。一种常见策略是优先考虑当前学习信号较强的能力，但在在线策略学习中，这些信号是内生的：过去的分配会改变策略，进而改变未来分配可用的证据。这可能形成一个反馈循环，使训练不足的能力获得越来越少的改进机会。我们通过配额-效率定律（Quota-Efficiency Law, QEL）将这一效应形式化，该定律表明，即使在各能力特定曝光量匹配的情况下，分配历史仍可能改变学习效率。受此启发，我们引入了 FEAST，一个无任务的自适应采样框架，它将机会分配与计算分配分离开来。FEAST 在保留各能力学习历史的同时动态发现能力聚类，并在各能力间维持持续的采样机会……
tldr: 论文提出了配额-效率定律（QEL），揭示在线策略学习中分配历史会影响学习效率，并据此引入 FEAST 框架，通过将机会分配与计算分配分离，实现无任务场景下公平而高效的自适应采样。
en_tdlr: The paper formalizes the Quota-Efficiency Law (QEL), showing that allocation history can change learning efficiency in on-policy learning, and introduces FEAST, a task-free adaptive sampling framework that separates opportunity allocation from compute allocation for fair and efficient learning.
